english.title: Cause / incite sexual activity with a mentally disordered male - no penetration - SOA 2003
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally caused or incited a

(A)_[man]_
(B)_[boy under the age of 18, namely **(..SPECIFY THE AGE..),]_

who was unable to refuse because of or for a reason related to a mental disorder, when you knew or could reasonably be expected to have known that he had such a disorder and that because of it, or for a reason related to it, he was likely to be unable to refuse, to engage in a sexual activity
english.legislation: Contrary to section 31(1) and (4) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 72 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by UK nationals / residents.
(ii) A person convicted of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 27).

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Fourteen years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
